title: Your Account Was Hacked or You Are Locked Out: What to Do First
html:
Work in this order. First, get back into the account if you are locked out. Second, find out what changed. Third, lock the account down. Fourth, protect your money and your other accounts. Each step below links to a guide that goes into detail.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. The steps are for a Google account. Other services have similar options under different names.

Sources last checked: 10 Oct 2026.

1. Get back in

If you cannot sign in, use the account recovery page and answer the questions as best you can. Google says wrong guesses do not lock you out of the process, there is no limit on attempts, and you cannot call Google for help signing in. If you lost your authenticator or phone, see lost authenticator recovery.

2. See what changed

In your Google Account, open Security and sign-in and select Review security events. Then open Your devices, choose Manage all devices, and look for devices you do not recognise. Sign them out. Check Gmail for forwarding rules and filters you did not create.

3. Lock it down

  • Change the password, and change it anywhere else you used the same one.
  • Turn on 2-Step Verification: which method to use.
  • Check recovery phone and email, and linked apps: Google account checklist.
  • Check whether the email or password has been in a breach: how to check.

4. Check the phone and protect your money

  • If your phone behaves strangely, or a stranger asked you to install an app: check your phone.
  • If you received a one-time code you did not ask for: what it can mean. Never read a code to a caller.
  • If money has moved, call your bank, then report on the helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in, as the Sanchar Saathi portal advises: fraud reporting steps.
  • If you think your number was moved to another SIM: SIM swap steps.

5. Tell people

If someone used your account to message others, tell your contacts not to click links or send money. Do not reply to messages that ask you to "verify" your account: see how to spot phishing.

What to do next

  1. Recover the account, then review devices and security events.
  2. Change passwords and turn on 2-Step Verification.
  3. Call your bank first if money or one-time codes are involved.

Sources

  • Secure a hacked or compromised Google Account (Google Account Help)
  • Recover your Google Account or Gmail (Google Account Help)
  • See devices that have used your Google Account (Google Account Help)
  • Chakshu: report suspected fraud communication (Sanchar Saathi)
